gdp_level.source: IMF World Economic Outlook (NGDP) · GDP at current prices, NT$ million, annual · actual years only. The IMF's figures for the years after the one shown are projections, which this site does not publish.
gdp_level.description: The total value of everything Taiwan produces in a year, at current prices. Annual only: Taiwan's quarterly national accounts are not available to automated downloads.
gdp_level.real: “Make it real” swaps this to the IMF's GDP at constant prices, also annual. This strips out the effect of price changes, so it shows genuine output growth rather than growth that's really just inflation.
gdp_level.dollar: “Dollarise” converts each year at its own NT$/US$ rate (Federal Reserve H.10, monthly average).

gdp_real.source: IMF World Economic Outlook (NGDP_R) · GDP at constant prices, NT$ million, annual · actual years only. The IMF's figures for the years after the one shown are projections, which this site does not publish.
gdp_real.description: GDP adjusted for inflation, so changes reflect real output growth rather than price changes.
gdp_real.real: This IS the “Make it real” series, toggling it off shows GDP at current (nominal) prices instead.
gdp_real.dollar: Same historical-rate matching as GDP (current prices): each year converted at its own NT$/US$ rate.

gdp_growth.source: IMF World Economic Outlook (NGDP_RPCH) · real GDP, change on the previous year, %, annual · actual years only. The IMF's figures for the years after the one shown are projections, which this site does not publish.
gdp_growth.description: How much the economy grew or shrank compared with the previous year, in real terms. Annual only on this page.
gdp_growth.real: This is already a real (inflation-adjusted) growth rate, “Make it real” has no additional effect on it.
gdp_growth.dollar: A growth rate (%) is currency-agnostic, converting the underlying New Taiwan dollars to dollars doesn't change the percentage change. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

cpi.source: IMF World Economic Outlook (PCPIPCH) · consumer prices, change in the annual average, %, annual · actual years only. The IMF's figures for the years after the one shown are projections, which this site does not publish.
cpi.description: How much consumer prices rose on average over the year compared with the year before. Annual only: monthly figures are not available to automated downloads.

unemployment.source: IMF World Economic Outlook (LUR) · unemployment rate, % of the labour force, annual · actual years only. The IMF's figures for the years after the one shown are projections, which this site does not publish.
unemployment.description: The share of the labour force that wants a job and is actively looking, but can't find one, averaged over the year.

policy_rate.source: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan), open data file WebF1 · discount rate (rate on rediscounts), by decision date, shown as the rate in force at the end of each month, from December 2000.
policy_rate.description: The rate the Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) charges on rediscounts, its headline policy rate. It moves in steps of one-eighth of a percentage point.

exports.source: IMF international trade in goods (ITG) · exports of goods, free on board, US$ converted to New Taiwan dollars at the Federal Reserve's monthly average rate (H.10), monthly.
exports.description: The value of goods Taiwan sells to the rest of the world each month, in New Taiwan dollars.
exports.dollar: Taiwan's customs figures are in US dollars; the NT$ shown are converted at each month's average rate, and “Dollarise” converts back.

imports.source: IMF international trade in goods (ITG) · imports of goods, cost, insurance and freight, US$ converted to New Taiwan dollars at the Federal Reserve's monthly average rate (H.10), monthly.
imports.description: The value of goods Taiwan buys from the rest of the world each month, in New Taiwan dollars.
imports.dollar: Taiwan's customs figures are in US dollars; the NT$ shown are converted at each month's average rate, and “Dollarise” converts back.

trade_balance.source: IMF international trade in goods (ITG) · exports (free on board) less imports (cost, insurance and freight), US$ converted to New Taiwan dollars at the Federal Reserve's monthly average rate (H.10), monthly.
trade_balance.description: Exports minus imports of goods each month. Above zero means Taiwan sells more abroad than it buys.
trade_balance.dollar: Taiwan's customs figures are in US dollars; the NT$ shown are converted at each month's average rate, and “Dollarise” converts back.

debt_gdp.source: IMF World Economic Outlook (GGXWDG_NGDP) · general government gross debt, % of GDP, annual · actual years only. The IMF's figures for the years after the one shown are projections, which this site does not publish.
debt_gdp.description: Everything government owes, across all levels of government, compared with the size of the economy.
debt_gdp.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

deficit.source: IMF World Economic Outlook (GGXCNL_NGDP) · general government net lending/borrowing, % of GDP, annual · actual years only. The IMF's figures for the years after the one shown are projections, which this site does not publish.
deficit.description: The yearly gap between government spending and revenue as a share of GDP; negative means a deficit. This covers all levels of government.
deficit.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

fx_usd.source: Federal Reserve H.10 daily rate (FRED DEXTAUS), averaged by month · shown as US$ per NT$100 (100 ÷ the published NT$ per US$).
fx_usd.description: How many US dollars NT$100 buys. A rising number means a stronger New Taiwan dollar.
